# The front door and About me

`/` is the front door. It has the archive's frame (a 212px rail and a main column) with me in the rail instead of the sessions, and one switch at the top between **Weekends** (the lead photo, then rows into Photographs and Things to try) and **Weekdays** (the resume and the side projects). The archive itself is `/photographs/`. The full write-up is in [docs/product-experience.md](../../../docs/product-experience.md#a-front-door-with-me-in-it-november-2026). The mocks it came from are `mocks/portfolio/` ([design-mocks](../design-mocks/SKILL.md)).

Since 2026-11-20 a full-screen **title screen** covers `/`: his name in pixel type over the tarn photo, with the summit rising between the words, three glass keys (Photographs, Things to try, Work) and small ones under them. Work opens the Weekdays side on the same page, and `/#weekdays` never shows it. Its write-up is [the title screen](../../../docs/product-experience.md#a-title-screen-over-the-front-door-november-2026), and its four rounds of mocks and verdicts are in design-mocks (`mocks/welcome/`).

## Rules

- **His words stay his.** The Weekends and Weekdays lines are what he wrote, with only typos fixed. Don't polish them. Resume lines are the PDF's, with job titles in sentence case.
- **No phone number or personal email** anywhere on the site, in `about.ts`, in the PDF or in the repo. `about.test.ts` checks the text. Contact is "Write to me", LinkedIn and GitHub.
- **Side projects are the three pinned on his GitHub**: this site, cozy-vibe-vids, balcFlights-LED. Each has a photo or a live element, never a link to something already on the site.
- **Say what it is and what it does.** The site, the README and the resume describe what he built and what it does. They don't credit AI agents, explain how AI was used to build it, or quote his messages to agents. Those messages stay in the skills' verdicts (2026-11-12).
- **Never change his resume.** Its words are his, so a new `public/Truman-Brown-Resume.pdf` only ever comes from a PDF he exported himself. The only edits to that file are the privacy and `?via=resume` fixes in "Update the resume", never its wording (2026-11-12).
- **The switch can't be missed.** Heading-size words, a tracked line under each saying what's behind it, a 2px bar.
- **Every "About me" goes to `/#weekdays`.** It works without script through `:target`, and `/about/`, `/work` and `/contact` redirect there. `/resume` and `/cv` redirect to `/Truman-Brown-Resume.pdf?via=typed`, so the open is counted and tagged.
- **The home description leads with my job,** because Google shows it under my name. The LinkedIn card shows only the og:title, the photo and the domain, and it reads well as 'Truman Brown' (checked in LinkedIn 2026-11-12), so leave the title alone.
- **The photo beside the front door is one he picked,** the red-eyed tree frog from Tapir Valley (`sitePhoto` in site.config.ts, 2026-11-15). It's both the share image (`og:image`, via `/api/og`) and Google's `primaryImageOfPage`, so the two hints agree. Change it there, never by pointing one hint somewhere else.
- **My name is the page's h1, once at a time.** The title screen's name is the h1 while it shows, and the name at the top of the rail is the h1 under it, styled as the archive's name. Only one is ever rendered, so screen readers and axe see one h1. Don't add another.
- **Don't link seattlebalc.com.** It's a friend's site that the radar reads from, not his work. The radar's link goes to the balcFlights-LED README, where a video shows the real panel. The privacy page still names the site in words, because visitors' browsers talk to it.
- **Photos he picked, not the first one.** The site project shows the newest session's header photo, chosen the way the session page chooses its banner (`banner`, then a wide cover, then the widest).
- **The resume is on the page, not only in the rail.** Resume (PDF) is the Weekdays side's one filled button, first in the row under his line. The rail lists it as a plain link with the others. Never two Resume buttons in different styles.
- **Every resume line shows.** No collapsing a job behind "N more": he found the button easy to miss.
- **The resume comes before the side projects.** Never suggest moving the projects up or trimming the resume to make room for them (see the 2026-11-09 verdict).
- **Counts read the same everywhere.** The Weekends row says "6 hobbies and a daily puzzle" through `thingsToTryLine` (`src/lib/hobbies.ts`), and photo counts get thousands separators. The site project dropped its counts line on 2026-11-27, since the Weekends side already shows them. The Weekdays role count is in the switch's count line only, not repeated over Work.
- **The icon is Mount Baker on the LED panel** (`public/favicon.svg`), picked from round 2 of the icon mocks (`mocks/portfolio/brand2.html`). Rules for it are in site-design.instructions.md. If the drawing changes, remake `public/favicon.ico` from it too (16, 32 and 48px PNGs in one ICO, made with sharp).
- **Tabs say his name first:** "Truman Brown", "Truman Brown | Work" while Weekdays shows, and "Truman Brown | <page>" everywhere else. He picked this over page-first, which reads better in a crowded tab strip.
- **Today's layout, sized up.** Round 2's three-column, two-page and projects-first layouts all crowded the page. What fixed the blank space was a wider rail (248px, the archive's stays 212px), one centered column the footer's width, bigger resume type (15px lines, 18px titles) and smaller project pictures. Since 2026-11-27 the projects sit three across in one row, each the same 3:2 picture with its name, one line in the Work rows' org style and one or two sentences, about 530px tall against Work's 1,440 at 1440 wide. The work should always take more room than the projects.
- **Same photo, never a different one,** when moving between pages. The lead photo is handed over by its URL and moves to its place. Nothing else carries over.
- **Weekdays is measured, so new parts get names.** The Analytics tab in `/admin` shows each visit to Weekdays: time on screen, how far down, clicks, copies and where they went next ([docs/analytics.md](../../../docs/analytics.md)). A new section needs `data-track-section`, and a new link or button on Weekdays or in the rail needs `data-track`, both named through `src/lib/track-names.ts`. `index.astro`'s `show()` must keep setting `door.dataset.side` and dispatching `week:side`, or the timer stops.
- **The PDF is served by a function.** `/Truman-Brown-Resume.pdf` is rewritten to `/api/resume`, which counts each open and serves a copy the build puts beside it. Replace only `public/Truman-Brown-Resume.pdf`; never link a different path to the resume. The PDF goes out first and the count runs a second after: never make the response wait on the lookup or the table, and keep the warm-up at a minute (lesson 7).
- **The resume's site links carry `?via=resume`** (`https://trumanbrown.com/?via=resume#weekdays` in the contact line, `https://trumanbrown.com/?via=resume` in the skills line). That's how the Analytics tab tells resume visits from typed ones. Keep both whenever the PDF is replaced.
- **The title screen never costs the resume path.** `/#weekdays` is where the resume and every About me link land, and it must download nothing of the title screen. Its pictures carry `data-src` and `data-srcset`, the inline script in TitleScreen.astro sets `title-ready` (and `title-on` unless the address is `/#weekdays`) and only then gives them their addresses, the Jersey fonts aren't preloaded and only apply under `html.title-on` (the noscript style sets them without script), and `initTitle` sets nothing up on `#weekdays` until the hash changes. After any change to `/`, list what `/#weekdays` requests (no `/title/` or `jersey` files) with the page arriving in two pieces, and run Lighthouse on both paths (lesson 8).
- **`src/lib/title/` imports only from itself.** Every shared chunk it pulls in is another round trip before the name can show (lesson 9). It keeps its own copies of the few helpers it needs, like `leaveForPage` and `ARRIVAL_KEY`, and `title.test.ts` checks that key still matches `LANDING_KEY`.
- **The title screen keeps its own look** (glass, Jersey pixel type, colours from the photo), the one exception in site-design.instructions.md. Its counts come from the same helpers as the Weekends rows, and Work's line is `ROLE` in `about.ts`.
- **The title screen ignores the theme.** The photo always shows at its own colours, and the name and the glass look the same in light and dark. The theme word isn't on the title screen, so a visitor can't change it there: "don't change the image based on dark or light mode, especially because user can't choose on main page. always make it the vibrant image colors" (2026-11-21, lesson 11). No `html.dark` rule belongs in TitleScreen.astro.
- **A new photo is a new folder.** `/title/*` is cached for a year as immutable, so new layers go in `tarn-v2` (or a new name) with a new `tarn.json`, never over the old files. The "i" is worked out at build time from the session's own order, so it follows the admin panel's display order and disappears if the photo leaves its session.
- **Read pixels off the main thread.** The glass tint and the name's fit read the photo. `getImageData` and `toDataURL` on a GPU-backed canvas stall the page while the GPU hands the pixels back, so downscale with `createImageBitmap` (`resizeWidth`) and draw any canvas that's read back with `willReadFrequently: true`, in idle time (lesson 10).

## Update the resume

1. Edit `WORK`, `SUMMARY`, `SCHOOL` or `SKILLS` in `src/lib/about.ts`, newest job first, months as `YYYY-MM`. His `WEEKDAYS` line quotes the migrated VM count ("over 47,000 VMs migrated today"), so when the first resume line's count changes, change that number too and nothing else in his line.
2. Replace the PDF. Open his new PDF with PyMuPDF (`pip install --target` a scratch folder) and read the contact line with `page.get_text()`. Since 2026-11-05 his own copy has no phone or email (`Seattle, WA | linkedin.com/in/trumanbrown | trumanbrown.com`). If one ever comes back, redact those spans and write the line back in the PDF's own embedded Cambria (`doc.extract_font`), keeping the links. Make sure both `trumanbrown.com` links end in `?via=resume` (`page.get_links()`, then set `link["uri"]` and `page.update_link(link)`), since his own copy may not have them. Either way, clear `creator` and `producer`, drop the XMP block (`del_xml_metadata`), check with `get_text()` and `strings` that no number or email is left, compare a render of the old and new page, and save it as `public/Truman-Brown-Resume.pdf`. If the text didn't change, `about.ts` doesn't need to: check each line is in the PDF word for word.
3. `npx vitest run src/lib/about.test.ts`, then look at `/#weekdays` at 1440×900 and 390×844.

## Add or change a side project

1. Edit `PROJECTS` in `src/lib/about.ts` and keep `about.test.ts`'s list in step.
2. A new `media` kind needs its own block in `Projects.astro`. Prefer something live and cheap: a build-time read of the site's own data, a third-party embed that loads only on a press, or a public API read only while on screen. A new host goes in the narrowest CSP directive in `staticwebapp.config.json` and on the privacy page.

## The radar

The panel draws what the real one does (`balc_flights_led/display.py` and `presentation.py` in his balcFlights-LED repo): the callsign as big as fits, type and altitude, speed and climb in the trend colour, compass point and distance on the right, dashed rings, a sweep at 85°/s, contacts brightest as the sweep passes, and the nearest with a trail and a blinking marker. The data is `https://seattlebalc.com/api/v1/flights` (no key, CORS `*`, cached 20 s, asks not to be polled harder). It's fetched only while the panel is on screen and the tab visible, every 20 s, with planes moved along their headings in between. Pause stops it, and reduced motion draws it still. `connect-src` allows `https://seattlebalc.com`.

The panel is never empty. Until the feed answers, when it fails, and whenever it has no planes in range, it flies `SAMPLE_FLIGHTS` from `radar.ts` (`sampleSnapshot`): seven planes on straight lines that leave past the range and come back round from the other side, so none jumps where it can be seen. The word beside Pause says "Sample" or "Live", and the screen-reader line says it's a sample. If it's always "Sample", `curl -s https://seattlebalc.com/api/v1/flights | head` first: on 2026-11-27 the feed answered `degraded` with `"source": "fallback-empty"` and no flights, which is what used to draw NO PLANES. A `degraded` status with flights draws the callsign in amber.

## Hard-won lessons

1. **The Windows `az` under WSL crashes printing Bicep** that has a `→` in it (`'charmap' codec can't encode`). Build with `--outfile` and a `wslpath -w` path instead of `--stdout`.
2. **A hidden VS Code browser panel skips view transitions** (`document.visibilityState` is `hidden`), and headless Chromium in WSL never paints after one. Check the handover by reading `.lead[data-current]` on both pages, and see the change in Windows Edge headless (site-motion lesson 13) or a visible browser.
3. **Local sessions have no `showcase` picks or captions,** so the lead photo is empty and the site project has no caption on a local build. Copy `src/content/sessions/*.json` aside, add picks for a look, and put them back.
4. **The first deploy failed on a duplicate route.** `/about` and `/about/` were both redirects, and Static Web Apps treats them as one route and refuses the whole config, which nothing local checked. One rule, `/about`, covers both, and `scripts/swa-config.test.mjs` fails on a repeat.
5. **The resume went missing by fixing a style.** Two Resume buttons in two styles drew "why is one off color", so the page's one was removed and only the rail's bottom-corner button stayed, which he then couldn't find. Fix a mismatch by matching the styles or demoting the duplicate to a link, not by removing the one in the obvious place.
6. **A browser test of the Weekdays beacon saw nothing at first.** `analytics.ts` sends nothing when `navigator.webdriver` is true, which Playwright sets, and the dev server never sends beacons. Test against `npm run build` and `astro preview`, override it with `addInitScript(() => Object.defineProperty(Navigator.prototype, 'webdriver', { get: () => false }))`, answer `/api/track` with `context.route` and read the bodies. Beacons sent as a page unloads never reach `route`, and bringing another tab forward doesn't hide a headless page, so to see what a hidden tab sends (speed, time on page, queued events) set `document.visibilityState` to `"hidden"` with `Object.defineProperty` and dispatch `visibilitychange`. Never do that against the live site, where it would log a fake visit (2026-11-09, `0773f1b`, `8632a5f`).
7. **The Resume button opened a blank tab for seconds.** `/api/resume` awaited the open's count before sending a byte: a place lookup that could wait two seconds, the Table SDK's first load and the write. The warm-up ping was meant to cover that, but its run history (`az rest` on the warmup Logic App's `runs`) showed every other ping taking five seconds, a fresh instance loading the lookup again, and the lookup's synchronous gunzip froze the whole process while it ran. Curl looked fast the whole time because it counts as a bot and skips the count, so time a real open's path from the code, not from curl. The PDF now goes out first, the gunzip runs off the main thread, and `api/resume/index.test.cjs` fails if the response waits on the lookup again (2026-11-17). The next morning it was still slow on his iPhone. Static Web Apps stops the Functions process after about five minutes without a request, the same as the old ping interval, so every ten minutes there was a gap where the next open waited for a new process. And the first count on any process loaded the Table SDK (half a second here, more on the Functions' disk) in the same process as the response. The ping now runs every minute and loads the Table SDK too, every deploy warms its new process, the count waits a second after the response, and a repeat open gets a 304. Static Web Apps still swaps in a new process now and then with no deploy (17:59 that day), so the front door sends an uncounted `HEAD` to the PDF once it loads, to wake it before anyone presses Resume. A 15-second probe of the bot path (curl, nothing recorded) beside the warm-up's run history is how to check it (2026-11-18).
8. **The title screen first made the resume path slower.** Hidden behind `#weekdays`, its photo and pixel fonts still downloaded: an eager `<img>` inside a `display: none` box still loads, preloads load regardless, and `:target` isn't applied early enough while the page parses, so the hidden screen was laid out and its fonts fetched. On a phone over slow 4G, `/#weekdays` went to a 4.8s largest paint. The fix is the rule above: addresses held in `data-*` until a CSP-hashed inline script, which runs after the stylesheets and before the first layout, says the screen will show (2026-11-20). That wasn't the whole of it. Once live, about one load of `/#weekdays` in three still fetched Jersey 25: the name is parsed before the inline script, and when the page arrives over a real network Chrome can style what it has so far before the script runs. A local server sends the whole page at once, so no local test saw it. The pixel fonts now apply only under `html.title-on`. To check, serve `/` in two pieces with a half-second pause just before the title screen's `<script>` and watch for `jersey` requests: the old build fetched it every time, the fixed one never.
9. **One import cost a second and a half.** `title.ts` first imported `open.ts` for the page change, which pulled the globe's code into the chunks the title screen waited on. Copying the twenty lines it needed into `src/lib/title/` took the phone's largest paint from 5.5s to 4.0s. Vite's dynamic `import()` would have added its preload helper chunk, so that's not a way around it either (2026-11-20).
10. **The glass froze the page for 684ms** on a phone-speed CPU (4x slowdown, as Lighthouse's phone runs). Its bent edges read each key's shape back from a canvas with `toDataURL`, and on a GPU-backed canvas that waits for the GPU. With `willReadFrequently: true` (a CPU canvas) and the work moved to idle time it takes 64ms, and the photo's tint and outline are read from small `createImageBitmap` copies instead of the full photo (2026-11-20).
11. **The live title screen was half as bright as the mock he approved.** The mock kit had a dark-theme "dusk" grade (`brightness(0.5) saturate(0.85)` on every photo layer, darker glass and outline) behind a switch that opened in light, so he never saw it. The port copied the kit's rules whole, and his browser runs dark, so the first thing he saw live was the dimmed photo. The title screen now has no dark rules at all, the glass tint no longer scales the photo's brightness for dark, and light and dark screenshots match pixel for pixel apart from the eagle. When a mock becomes a page, carry over only what he looked at, and look at the live page in dark as well as light (2026-11-21).
